title: Global optimization of Lipschitz nonconvex functions with exact values
summary: Find an approximate global minimizer of the unknown objective over $X$. Evaluate the final recommendation by simple regret $f(\widehat{x})-\min_{u\in X}f(u)$; losses incurred during queries are not accumulated.

description_paragraphs: Find an approximate global minimizer of the unknown objective over $X$. Evaluate the final recommendation by simple regret $f(\widehat{x})-\min_{u\in X}f(u)$; losses incurred during queries are not accumulated.

domain_roles.function: A given compact convex set X contained in R^d with nonempty interior.
domain_roles.localization: X is the optimization domain itself; no additional localization of an unconstrained global minimizer is promised.

description_paragraphs: $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is known, compact and convex, with nonempty interior. The objective $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_2$; convexity is not assumed.
At any finite query point $x$ in $X$, the oracle returns the single exact scalar $f(x)$. The reply is uniquely determined and contains no gradient, subgradient or derivative-vector product.

The public inputs are $d$, $L$, $X$, $\varepsilon$, $T$, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

Return $\widehat{x}\in X$. The output may be an unqueried point, a random choice among previous points, or an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

metric.native_metric_wording: The base loss is $\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*$, where $f_*=\inf_{u\in X}f(u)$. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance $\varepsilon$.

accounting.free_operations: Only the public operations explicitly stated in this specification are free. Operations accessing the unknown instance provide no free information.

description_paragraphs: Each scalar function value or noisy observation costs $1$ call. Every location in a multipoint finite difference, every initialization query, and every reference observation is charged.
Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

guarantees.probability_space: The algorithm's private seed; the instance is fixed and determines each oracle response uniquely.
description_paragraphs: After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. Require $\mathbb{E}[\ell(I,\widehat{x})]\le \varepsilon$, fixing the instance before averaging over algorithmic and feedback randomness.
Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.
